verses.text: After many days, when Yahweh had given rest to Israel from their enemies all around, and Joshua was old and well advanced in years,
Joshua called for all Israel, for their elders and for their heads, and for their judges and for their officers, and said to them, “I am old and well advanced in years.
You have seen all that Yahweh your God has done to all these nations because of you; for it is Yahweh your God who has fought for you.

Behold, I have allotted to you these nations that remain, to be an inheritance for your tribes, from the Jordan, with all the nations that I have cut off, even to the great sea toward the going down of the sun.
Yahweh your God will thrust them out from before you, and drive them from out of your sight. You shall possess their land, as Yahweh your God spoke to you.
“Therefore be very courageous to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, that you not turn aside from it to the right hand or to the left;
that you not come among these nations, these that remain among you; neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow down yourselves to them;
but hold fast to Yahweh your God, as you have done to this day.
“For Yahweh has driven great and strong nations out from before you. But as for you, no man has stood before you to this day.
One man of you shall chase a thousand; for it is Yahweh your God who fights for you, as he spoke to you.
Take good heed therefore to yourselves, that you love Yahweh your God.
“But if you do at all go back, and hold fast to the remnant of these nations, even these who remain among you, and make marriages with them, and go in to them, and they to you;

know for a certainty that Yahweh your God will no longer drive these nations from out of your sight; but they shall be a snare and a trap to you, a scourge in your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from off this good land which Yahweh your God has given you.

“Behold, today I am going the way of all the earth. You know in all your hearts and in all your souls that not one thing has failed of all the good things which Yahweh your God spoke concerning you. All have happened to you. Not one thing has failed of it.

It shall happen that as all the good things have come on you of which Yahweh your God spoke to you, so Yahweh will bring on you all the evil things, until he has destroyed you from off this good land which Yahweh your God has given you,

when you disobey the covenant of Yahweh your God, which he commanded you, and go and serve other gods, and bow down yourselves to them. Then Yahweh’s anger will be kindled against you, and you will perish quickly from off the good land which he has given to you.”

footnotes.content: An old man looks around and sees peace—truly peace—where there was only struggle. Joshua has earned the right to lay down the weight. The Lord had promised rest; now He keeps it. This quiet, earned moment is its own kind of victory.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua calls everyone—elders, leaders, judges, officers. No one is left out of this farewell. He doesn't hand off power secretly; he gathers the whole people to speak face-to-face. A leader's last word is offered plainly, to all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'You have seen' — Joshua appeals to their own eyes. They remember the miracles, the walls, the victories. He doesn't ask them to believe on faith alone; he anchors them in what they know they witnessed. The Lord *showed* them who He is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The promised land wasn't handed to them complete and conquered. Joshua reminds them: you still have work to do, territory to possess. The Lord's inheritance to us often comes with a threshold we still must cross. Grace does not remove our calling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He promises God's continued power—'will thrust them out.' But it rests on a condition that isn't yet spoken: obedience. The Lord's promises are sure, but they are not unconditional. What we keep is bound to what we guard.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Keep and do all that is written in the book of the law' — Joshua speaks of a *written* law, something fixed and knowable. Not customs, not guesses. The word of God is firm ground to stand on; the danger is not knowing it, but straying from it deliberately.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't even speak the names of their gods. Joshua knows how seductive other faiths can be—a word becomes a thought, a thought becomes a compromise. He sets a boundary of speech itself, because the tongue leads the heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Hold fast to Yahweh your God, as you have done to this day.' Joshua appeals to their track record. You *know* how to cleave to Him; you've tasted His faithfulness. This is not a new command, but a remembrance and a call to persist.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No enemy has stood before Israel. Not because Israel is mighty—because God fights. Joshua stirs their memory of His power, not to boast, but to remind them: *This* is who you belong to. Lean into that, not away from it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One man chases a thousand—the proportion is absurd, which is exactly the point. The math doesn't work unless the Lord multiplies their strength. Courage isn't the absence of fear; it's relying on a power greater than the enemy's.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Take good heed therefore to yourselves, that you love Yahweh your God.' After all the commands, Joshua returns to the root: love. The Deuteronomic heart. Obedience flows from love; without it, keeping rules becomes empty. He asks them to guard their affection.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Intermarriage with the pagan peoples—a practical warning with spiritual teeth. When we blur the boundaries, when we join ourselves to those who serve other gods, the compromise becomes woven into our children. Joshua sees how quickly inheritance can be lost through the intimate.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The same nations left behind, once Israel's victory, become a snare and thorns. Nothing changes but Israel's posture toward God. The land remains 'good'—but what feels good becomes a trap when trust falters. Joshua speaks as one who knows how grace can be lost through carelessness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Not one thing has failed.' Joshua points to God's perfect faithfulness—every promise fulfilled. This is the testimony of an entire generation. He holds up the *record*: look, the Lord has kept His word. Now will you keep yours?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As the good has come, so judgment will come. Symmetry, not spite. The Lord is as faithful in warning as in blessing. Joshua speaks of consequences not to frighten but to clarify: faithfulness brings life; unfaithfulness, death. The choice is real.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in Joshua's final word: the covenant holds. Break it, and destruction follows swiftly. But the covenant itself—the bond of love with the Lord—stands open. Every generation must choose, as Israel did, whether to cleave or to turn away. The choice remains ours.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
